doc.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Marriage, Chicago and arriving in New York
title: Jimmy's advice: be yourself and count your blessings
summary: She was a nervous speaker at the Embers until Jimmy's advice to be herself helped; he also told her to count her blessings when she was depressed.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: It’s funny. You don’t have to have this on the tape. I used to be a nervous wreck about speaking. I couldn’t say anything. When I opened at the Embers . . . because Jimmy was always the front man, always doing the talking. I never did get to say a word. He didn’t coach me or anything. So when . . . by the time I got my own group, I couldn’t say anything. So here I am at the Embers. I’m really having a hard job just saying, “Thank you, ladies and gentlemen. Now we’d like to present Eddie Heywood.” I had it written on a piece of paper. Now, years later, I’m so voluble, you can’t stop me. It’s just the total . . . Jimmy would always say, “Be yourself. Just be yourself. Don’t try to be anything fancy.”
That’s very good advice, because there’s . . .
It took me a long time to keep it.
That’s what all of us should do. If we followed those rules, I think a lot of things would fall in place, musically and otherwise.

God, and he . . . Jimmy left me with all these good things, like I would be saying, “I’m so depressed. God, I can’t get out of this mood.” He’d say, “Count your blessings. Think of all the things you have in your favor. You’ve got talent, and you’ve got money in the bank, and you’ve got me, and you’ve go friends.” He would go through all these things.
Said especially him, right? [laughs] That’s a good . . . That’s right. That’s true. It should be.

Actually he didn’t say that. I would be the one that would say that. He would list all these other good things, but it was always, “Count your blessings. Be thankful.” Those were the things. Always be thankful for everything you have. Don’t . . . How can you be depressed? So, anyway . . .
